reproduction_target: A computational framework that uses single-cell whole-genome sequencing (scWGS) to separate ONGOING chromosomal instability (CIN) from HISTORICAL CIN, by (i) detecting cell-unique copy number alterations and (ii) probabilistically mapping each individual copy number event to one of the 17 published CIN signatures. Computational target: BWA-MEM single-end alignment to GRCh37 and samtools-markdup duplicate marking; QDNAseq 100 kb read counting with GC/mappability correction and centromere/sex-chromosome exclusion; absolute copy number fitting over a 1.5-8 ploidy range at purity fixed to 1 with an RMSD selection criterion, 15-reads-per-bin-per-copy downsampling, a star quality rating and MANUAL review/adjustment of fitting solutions; single-cell noise and breakpoint QC filters; the cell-unique CNA classifier (window-based segment-boundary homogenisation, clonal >=90% / shared / unique classification, null-distribution significance test built from 81,464 segments across 1,441 cells); the downsampling analysis relating cell sampling fraction to temporal resolution; the redefined copy number feature embedding and the probabilistic per-event signature assignment; the in silico simulation validation over 1,000 simulated samples; YAPSA linear-combination-decomposition quantification of CIN signature activities on TCGA (ASCAT) and Hartwig (PURPLE) profiles; FACETS absolute copy number calling from MSK-IMPACT tumour-normal pairs; the Wilcoxon rank-sum / paired signed-rank comparisons; drc dose-response curve fitting for organoid ED50; and DECODR v3.0 analysis of Sanger traces for CRISPR clone validation. Patient-derived pancreatic organoid culture, CRISPR-Cas9 knockout generation in hTERT RPE-1 Cas9 cells, immunoblotting, PCR/Sanger bench work, DNA extraction + bulk low-pass WGS library prep and NovaSeq X Plus sequencing, single-cell isolation (cellenONE) with PicoPLEX Gold / mDLP+ library preparation, and the drug treatment / CellTiter-Glo viability assays are wet-lab (W, out of scope for computational reproduction).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis list built from the bioRxiv v1 full-text HTML (https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.11.26.690781v1.full), fetched with curl + browser user-agent into an isolated per-paper scratch directory (/tmp/stage1_10.1101_2025.11.26.690781, 345 KB HTML -> 77 KB extracted text). FETCH NOTE: the JATS source XML endpoint returned HTTP 403 via WebFetch and Cloudflare error 1015 (rate limit) via curl on two attempts; the Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint returns 404 for this preprint (PPR1126529) and the Europe PMC PDF link is expired. The v1 full-text HTML was used instead and carries the complete Methods. Title phrase 'Tracking ongoing chromosomal instability' and the full abstract were confirmed present in the fetched text, so the fetch is the correct paper. Two supplements that carry load-bearing method detail could NOT be read: Methods Table S1 ('Sources of data used in this study', rendered only as a 'View this table' stub in the HTML, no accession strings anywhere in the 345 KB document) and Supplementary Note 1 (the full development and in silico validation of the redefined copy number encoding), which the paper itself says 'will be publicly available upon publication'. Both the Code availability and the Data availability statements are forward-looking promises: 'The source code for reproducing analyses and figures will be available upon publication.' and 'All data required for reproducing these analyses will be available upon publication. Raw data generated in this study will be deposited in the European Genome-phenome Archive (EGA) upon publication.' No repository URL for this paper's own code appears anywhere. The only two URLs in the whole manuscript are third-party: https://github.com/VanLoo-lab/ascat (source of the downloaded TCGA ASCAT copy number profiles) and https://decodr.org/ (the DECODR v3.0 web tool). Code axis is scored 1 ('described / custom-not-deposited but reconstructable') where a public tool is named and the procedure is operationally described, and 0 where the paper explicitly defers the method detail to a not-yet-released supplement or where the step is a manual/closed-service operation; it is never 2, because no code is deposited. Version follows the sibling-report convention: exact prose pin -> 1 with subtier exact_pins_partial (Stage-1 ceiling, no environment closure), tool named but unversioned -> 1 with subtier floating, no tool named at all -> 0. Wet-lab steps counted in W with verdict OOS, not verdicted.

steps.label: Read alignment: 'Reads were aligned as single-end against the human genome assembly GRCh37 using BWA-MEM (v0.7.17)' - exact version pin, genome build named, but no reference FASTA source/accession, no BWA flags beyond single-end, and the primary inputs (this study's bulk lpWGS and scWGS reads) are not yet deposited (EGA promised 'upon publication')
Duplicate marking: 'Duplicate reads were then identified and marked using samtools-markdup (v1.15)' - exact version pin, no flags stated, same undeposited input data

Binned read counting and bias correction with the QDNAseq R package: reads counted in 100 kb bins, bins on centromeres and undefined-sequence regions of hg19 excluded, sex chromosomes excluded, counts corrected for mappability and GC content - no QDNAseq version, no bin annotation object/release named, no blacklist file identified, and the segmentation algorithm applied after counting is never named

Absolute copy number fitting: ploidy searched over 1.5 < ploidy < 8 (narrowed to +/-0.5 when ploidy known from flow cytometry / propidium iodide), purity fixed at 1, samples downsampled to 15 reads per bin per chromosome copy with samples below that depth excluded, solution chosen by lowest RMSD between non-rounded and rounded copy numbers 'as previously described(33)' - and then 'Fitting solutions were manually reviewed and adjusted if necessary', an unrecorded manual intervention with no tool, no version and no log of which samples were adjusted

Single-cell profile QC and segment post-processing: star rating 'as previously described(16,33)' with 1-star samples discarded; cells excluded if the standard deviation of bin counts exceeds the median across all cells; cells excluded if breakpoint count exceeds two standard deviations above the mean across all non-noisy cells; segment copy numbers rounded to nearest integer and adjacent equal segments merged - thresholds explicit but no script, no tool and no version

Cell-unique copy number alteration identification: window-based smoothing to homogenise segment boundaries across cells, rounding to integer, classification as clonal (present in >=90% of cells), shared (>1 cell) or unique (1 cell), plus a significance test of the observed copy number deviation against a null distribution computed from 81,464 segments across 1,441 cells - explicitly incomplete: 'Further details of the heuristic approach applied to ensure robust classification of unique copy number alterations will be available upon publication.' No window size, no significance cutoff, no code

Downsampling analysis relating cell sampling fraction to temporal resolution of unique events (Figure 1c): cells randomly selected 20 times per sample from three TNBC tumours and two TNBC cell lines of Minussi et al. 2021 with >10 passing single-cell profiles - the sampling fractions grid is not stated, no random seed is given and the sampling code is not deposited

Probabilistic mapping of individual copy number events to CIN signatures: the published CIN signature framework(4) adapted by redefining the copy number feature embedding space to allow per-event assignment from rounded 100 kb-resolution profiles, with three copy number features extracted per event and the highest-probability signature assigned; the candidate signature set per sample is the bulk signature set complemented by signatures detected across all single cells - the core of the paper, and the paper states 'The full details of the development and in silico validation of the redefined encoding framework are outlined in Supplementary Note 1, which will be publicly available upon publication.' No feature definitions, no probability model, no signature reference matrix version, no code

In silico validation of the signature mapping approach: copy number alterations from known signatures simulated for 1,000 samples, reported accuracy 82.07% (range 67.5-95.7% across signatures; Figure 1e, Supplementary Figure 3) - the simulator, its parameters, its random seed and the simulated datasets are all in the deferred Supplementary Note 1; nothing is currently obtainable

CIN signature activity quantification on bulk cohorts: genome-wide distributions of the 3 copy number features computed per profile, then activities quantified with the linear combination decomposition (LCD) function of the YAPSA R package 'as previously described(63)', applied to 60 primary TNBCs (ASCAT-derived TCGA profiles downloaded from https://github.com/VanLoo-lab/ascat, triple-negative status required to agree across three annotation sources) and 119 metastatic TNBCs (PURPLE-derived Hartwig profiles); activities scaled within primary and metastatic sets to enable cross-cohort comparison - YAPSA unversioned, signature reference matrix not identified, scaling method not defined, HMF access restricted with no accession or data-request identifier

Genome-wide absolute copy number calling from MSK-IMPACT targeted panel tumour-normal pairs with FACETS(65), for 82 TNBC tumours comprising 39 matched primary-metastatic pairs; when a patient had multiple samples 'we retained the profile with the highest quality and/or purity' - no FACETS version, no FACETS parameters (cval, snp-pileup settings, purity/ploidy constraints), and the retention rule is stated only in that ambiguous form; MSK clinical/processed/raw data have restricted access with no accession

Statistical comparisons of CIN signature activities: Wilcoxon rank-sum test between primary and metastatic TNBC cohorts (CX signatures), paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test for CX10 between the 39 matched primary-metastasis MSK pairs - tests and pairing explicitly named, but no software or package is named anywhere, no multiple-testing correction is stated, and the underlying activity tables are not deposited

Dose-response curve fitting for the pancreatic organoid oxaliplatin screen: 'Drug-response curves were fitted using the R package drc(60) to estimate ED50 values for each organoid', concentration range extended to 100 uM for model fitting, and ED50 assigned to the highest fitted concentration when viability did not drop by more than 20% - no drc version, no model/curve family (LL.4 etc.) named, no normalisation detail, and the per-well luminescence source data are not deposited (only Supplementary Figure 2)

CRISPR editing confirmation from Sanger traces with DECODR v3.0(57) (https://decodr.org/) on PCR amplicons of the targeted TP53, BRCA1 and BRCA2 loci - exact tool version and a live URL, but DECODR is a hosted closed web service (no source, no local execution path), no analysis settings are stated, and the Sanger trace files are not deposited

Patient-derived pancreatic adenocarcinoma organoid culture: five organoids from surgical resections at Hospital Clinico Universitario Virgen de la Arrixaca under IRB protocol CEIC HCUVA-2013/01, grown in Matrigel and recovered with TrypLE Express

CRISPR-Cas9 knockout cell line generation: hTERT RPE-1 Cas9 cells, sgRNAs against TP53 exon 4, BRCA1 exon 12 and BRCA2 exon 11, tracrRNA annealing programme, Lipofectamine RNAiMAX transfection, single-clone sorting on a cellenONE piezo-electric dispenser and clone expansion
Immunoblotting for knockout validation (HEPES/NP-40 lysis, NuPAGE 3-8% Tris-Acetate, PVDF transfer, anti-p53 DO-1, anti-GAPDH, HRP secondaries, ChemiDoc imaging)
Genomic DNA extraction, locus PCR with the listed TP53/BRCA1/BRCA2 primers, gel purification and Sanger sequencing at the CNIO Genomics Unit

Bulk low-pass WGS: DNA extraction from 5 million-cell pellets (DNeasy), Quant-iT PicoGreen quantification, Illumina DNA Prep library construction with IDT for Illumina UD indexes, LabChip fragment sizing, equimolar pooling and NovaSeq X Plus sequencing targeting 10 million reads per fresh-frozen sample

Single-cell WGS: palbociclib G1 arrest (1 uM, 16 h), cellenONE image-based single-cell dispensing into 96-well plates (3-6 plates per model, gated on diameter/elongation/circularity), then either SMARTer PicoPLEX Gold single-cell DNA-seq or the modified DLP+ (mDLP+) protocol with protease lysis, Nextera XT tagmentation, Equinox amplification and UD index adapters (14 PCR cycles)

Drug treatments and viability assays: doxorubicin 5 nM for 10 population doublings (refreshed every 3 days) on hTERT RPE-1 Cas9 TP53-/-; olaparib and rucaparib dose series (0.1-5 uM, 6 days) with CellTiter-Glo on an EnVision reader; oxaliplatin (0.003-50 uM) on 4 pancreatic organoids in Matrigel with CellTiter-Glo at 96 h

headline.static_readiness: 0/14 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification); unexecuted, and here there is no declared environment to validate at all, so n_exact_capture_unexecuted = 0 and n_fetch_required = 0
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 1/14 computational steps (C10, YAPSA linear-combination-decomposition of CIN signature activities on TCGA/Hartwig bulk profiles) - it reaches RI only because the input profiles are third-party and at least partly resolvable (TCGA ASCAT profiles at https://github.com/VanLoo-lab/ascat, HTTP 200; Hartwig under documented restricted access), a public package is named, and the procedure is described well enough to reconstruct. The other 13/14 steps cap at NI. Three distinct blockers dominate, and they are structural rather than incidental. (1) No code exists to inspect: 'The source code for reproducing analyses and figures will be available upon publication.' - no repository URL, DOI or archive for this paper's code appears anywhere in the manuscript. (2) The primary data are not deposited: 'Raw data generated in this study will be deposited in the European Genome-phenome Archive (EGA) upon publication.' - no EGA accession, no embargo date, and no accession string of any kind (GSE/SRP/PRJ/EGAS/EGAD/phs) occurs in the 345 KB full-text document; every step that consumes this study's own scWGS or bulk lpWGS reads therefore scores data=0. (3) The two novel algorithmic contributions - the unique-event calling heuristic and the redefined per-event signature encoding - are explicitly deferred: 'Further details of the heuristic approach ... will be available upon publication' and 'Supplementary Note 1, which will be publicly available upon publication'. C8 and C9, the methodological core of the paper, score 0 on all four axes. Only three exact version pins exist in the entire manuscript (BWA-MEM v0.7.17, samtools-markdup v1.15, DECODR v3.0); QDNAseq, YAPSA, FACETS and drc are named without versions, and no R version, no operating system, no conda environment, no lockfile and no container image is mentioned. capture_claim is therefore 'exact_pins_partial' and, under collection protocol v0.2.6, stage2_candidate is false: a code check could not raise version above 1 for this paper because there is no environment closure to verify (and, at present, no code to fetch).
headline.coverage: 14 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 full-text Methods prose (alignment, duplicate marking, QDNAseq binning, absolute copy number fitting, single-cell QC, unique-event calling, the downsampling temporal-resolution analysis, per-event signature mapping, the in silico simulation validation, YAPSA activity quantification on TCGA/Hartwig, FACETS on MSK-IMPACT, the Wilcoxon comparisons, drc dose-response fitting, DECODR v3.0 Sanger analysis). 7 wet-lab step groups counted in W but out of computational-reproduction scope: organoid culture, CRISPR-Cas9 knockout generation, immunoblotting, PCR/Sanger bench work, bulk low-pass WGS library prep + NovaSeq X Plus sequencing, single-cell isolation + PicoPLEX Gold / mDLP+ scWGS library prep, and the drug treatment / CellTiter-Glo viability assays. Computational coverage = 14/21 = 67%. Coverage caveat: Methods Table S1 ('Sources of data used in this study') renders only as a 'View this table' stub in the fetched HTML and could not be read, and Supplementary Note 1 is not yet released, so the data-source list and the encoding-framework specification are both outside what this Stage-1 read could inspect.

gaps.where: Whole analysis pipeline - section 'Data reporting and code availability', verbatim: 'The source code for reproducing analyses and figures will be available upon publication.'
gaps.missing: No code is deposited or linked. A full-text search of the 345 KB v1 HTML for 'github', 'gitlab', 'bitbucket', 'zenodo' and 'software heritage' returns exactly one GitHub URL, https://github.com/VanLoo-lab/ascat, which is a THIRD-PARTY source of downloaded TCGA ASCAT copy number profiles, not this paper's code. This covers the copy number fitting wrapper (C4), the single-cell QC filters (C5), the unique-event caller (C6), the downsampling analysis (C7), the per-event signature mapper (C8), the simulator (C9), the YAPSA/FACETS driver scripts (C10, C11) and all figure code.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the framework (unique-event calling, feature encoding, probabilistic signature assignment) and the downstream analysis/figure scripts in a public repository with a tagged release or Zenodo DOI, and replace the promise in the availability statement with a resolvable URL.

gaps.where: C6 'Identifying cell-unique copy number alterations' and C8 'Mapping signatures to individual copy number segments' - the two novel algorithmic contributions
gaps.missing: Both are declared incomplete in the manuscript itself. C6: 'Further details of the heuristic approach applied to ensure robust classification of unique copy number alterations will be available upon publication.' - no smoothing window size, no significance threshold for the null-distribution test, no handling of ties or of adjacent-segment merging order. C8: the redefined copy number feature embedding space, the three per-event features, the probability model and the signature reference matrix are all deferred to Supplementary Note 1. Without these, the central claim of the paper (separating ongoing from historical CIN) cannot be re-derived from the text at all.
gaps.how_to_close: Release Supplementary Note 1 and the heuristic specification together with reference implementations, and state the window size, the significance cutoff and the signature reference matrix version inline in the Methods.

gaps.where: C8, C9 - Supplementary Note 1; and the data-source list - Methods Table S1
gaps.missing: The development and in silico validation of the redefined encoding framework are externalised to Supplementary Note 1, which 'will be publicly available upon publication'. Methods Table S1 ('Sources of data used in this study and their respective sources') is referenced as the authoritative list of every dataset used, but renders only as a 'View this table' stub in the full-text HTML and could not be inspected in this Stage-1 read; no accession identifier of any type appears in the retrievable text, so it is not possible to confirm from the paper which specific archives the Watson et al. 2024 and Minussi et al. 2021 datasets were pulled from.
gaps.how_to_close: Release Supplementary Note 1 with the preprint rather than at journal publication, and reproduce the Methods Table S1 rows (dataset, source archive, accession, version/date of download) as machine-readable text in the Methods or as a deposited supplementary file.

gaps.where: Data availability - all data generated in this study (bulk low-pass WGS and scWGS of hTERT RPE-1 Cas9 TP53-/-, TP53-/-BRCA1-/-, TP53-/-BRCA2-/- clones, and of the five patient-derived pancreatic organoids including the diploid/tetraploid clone pair)
gaps.missing: Verbatim: 'All data required for reproducing these analyses will be available upon publication. Raw data generated in this study will be deposited in the European Genome-phenome Archive (EGA) upon publication.' No EGA study or dataset accession, no DOI and no embargo release date is given, so the primary input to C1-C6, C13 and C14 is currently unobtainable. The drug-sensitivity luminescence tables behind the drc fits (C13) and the Sanger traces behind DECODR (C14) are not mentioned in the availability statement at all.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the scWGS and bulk lpWGS data with resolvable EGA accessions (EGAS/EGAD) plus a documented Data Access Committee route, and add supplementary tables for the per-well CellTiter-Glo measurements and the Sanger trace files.

gaps.where: C10 (Hartwig Medical Foundation metastatic TNBC cohort, n=119) and C11 (MSK-IMPACT primary-metastasis pairs, n=82 tumours / 39 patients)
gaps.missing: Verbatim: 'The Hartwig Medical Foundation (HMF) clinical, processed and raw sequencing data have restricted access. The Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK) clinical, processed and raw sequencing data have restricted access.' Access is by institutional agreement (the Acknowledgements state the study used data 'that Hartwig Medical Foundation has made available to the study through the Hartwig Medical Database'), not through a stated accession with a documented request identifier. Under the rubric's controlled-access rule this is data=1 rather than data=2 precisely because no resolvable identifier is given, not because the gating itself is illegitimate.
gaps.how_to_close: State the HMF data request identifier (DR-number) and the MSK cohort/IRB identifier, plus the exact release version of each dataset used, so a licensed third party can request the identical extract.

gaps.where: Every computational step - whole software environment
gaps.missing: Only three exact version pins occur in the entire manuscript: BWA-MEM v0.7.17 (C1), samtools-markdup v1.15 (C2) and DECODR v3.0 (C14). QDNAseq (C3), YAPSA (C10), FACETS (C11) and drc (C13) are named with a citation but no version. No R version, no Python version, no operating system, no conda/renv environment file, no lockfile and no container image is mentioned anywhere. This is the reason capture_claim is 'exact_pins_partial' rather than 'env_lock_claimed', and it is what caps the paper below R-star independently of the missing code.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock / renv.lock / pixi.lock or a container digest pinning the interpreter and every package (QDNAseq and its bin annotations, YAPSA, FACETS, drc, plus whatever implements the unique-event caller and the signature mapper), and add a versions table to the Methods.

gaps.where: C1, C3, C8, C10 - reference resources
gaps.missing: The genome assembly is named as 'GRCh37' for alignment and 'hg19' for the excluded-bin annotation without stating which FASTA release, patch level or provider was used, nor the QDNAseq bin-annotation object version. The centromere / undefined-sequence exclusion list is not identified. The CIN signature compendium is cited (17 signatures, ref 4) but no version or file for the signature reference matrix is given, and no version is given for the TCGA ASCAT profile release downloaded from the VanLoo-lab repository (a moving repository head, not a tagged release) or for the Hartwig PURPLE output release.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin the reference genome release and provider, the QDNAseq bin-annotation version, the exclusion BED file, the signature matrix file with a checksum, and the exact commit/tag or release date of the downloaded ASCAT and PURPLE profile sets.

gaps.where: C7 (downsampling analysis, Figure 1c) and C9 (in silico validation over 1,000 simulated samples, Figure 1e)
gaps.missing: Both steps are stochastic and no random seed is reported. C7: 'For each sample, cells were randomly selected 20 times' - the set of sampling fractions on the x-axis is not stated either. C9: alterations 'were simulated for 1,000 samples' with the generator, its parameters and its seed all deferred to Supplementary Note 1. The reported 82.07% accuracy (range 67.5-95.7%) therefore cannot be reproduced exactly, only distributionally, even once code appears.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the seed (and show it is consumed by the code), the sampling-fraction grid, the number of replicates and the simulation parameter set; deposit the simulated datasets alongside the generator.

gaps.where: C7, and the reanalysis of external scWGS cohorts (Watson et al. 2024 hTERT-HMEC reversine clones, n=41; Minussi et al. 2021 TNBC cohort, 8 patients)
gaps.missing: The paper says it 'downloaded publicly available sequencing data' for both cohorts and cites the source publications, but no accession is given in the retrievable text and the sample-to-file correspondence is delegated to Methods Table S1, which could not be read. Ploidy selection for these cohorts is said to follow the original authors' propidium iodide / flow cytometry measurements, but the per-sample ploidy values actually used are not tabulated, and C4 narrows the fitting range to +/-0.5 around them - so the fits are not re-derivable without that table.
gaps.how_to_close: List the accessions and the exact run/cell identifiers used from each external cohort, together with the per-sample ploidy value applied and the list of cells that passed the C5 QC filters.

gaps.where: C4 - absolute copy number fitting, verbatim: 'Fitting solutions were manually reviewed and adjusted if necessary.'
gaps.missing: A manual, non-scripted intervention sits inside the primary data-processing path and is not recorded anywhere: which samples were adjusted, what the adjustment was, and by what criterion. No amount of released code closes this gap unless the adjustments themselves are logged; it makes the copy number profiles - the input to every downstream step - irreproducible by re-execution alone.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the final fitted profiles (per sample: ploidy, purity, segment table) together with a log of every manual adjustment and its rationale, so downstream steps can be re-run from a fixed, inspectable intermediate.

gaps.where: C14 - DECODR v3.0 (https://decodr.org/), used to confirm CRISPR editing from Sanger traces
gaps.missing: DECODR is a hosted, closed web service. The version is exactly pinned (v3.0) and the URL resolves (HTTP 200 on 2026-07-28), but there is no source code, no local execution path and no stated analysis settings; results depend on whatever the service runs at request time. The input Sanger traces are also not deposited.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the Sanger .ab1 traces and the DECODR result exports as supplementary files so the editing calls can be checked without re-invoking the hosted service.

gaps.where: W1-W7 - organoid culture, CRISPR knockout generation, immunoblotting, PCR/Sanger, bulk lpWGS library prep + NovaSeq X Plus sequencing, single-cell isolation + PicoPLEX Gold / mDLP+ library prep, drug treatments and CellTiter-Glo viability assays
gaps.missing: Non-computational steps, out of scope for computational reproduction (counted in W = 7, verdict OOS). Recorded here only so the denominator is auditable; the wet-lab prose is in fact unusually detailed (catalogue numbers, concentrations, thermocycler programmes, sgRNA and primer sequences are all given).
gaps.how_to_close: n/a - OOS. The wet-lab description is already at protocol level; depositing the resulting sequencing data (gap type 5 above) is what would connect it to the computational chain.
